source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: 'What the body does to the drug' describes:
questions.rationale: Pharmacokinetics is drug movement: absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion. Pharmacodynamics is what the drug does to the body.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Pharmacology Terms (PDF p. 105)
questions.quote: What the body does to the drug

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Biotransformation of a drug is also called:
questions.rationale: Metabolism (biotransformation) inactivates drugs, mainly in the liver.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, ADME (PDF p. 105)
questions.quote: Also known as Biotransformation

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: An undesired, abnormal drug response more severe than a side effect is a(n):
questions.rationale: Adverse reactions are undesired, more severe than side effects, abnormal, and reportable.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Therapeutic Index (PDF p. 105)
questions.quote: More severe than side effects

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which clinical trial phase establishes whether a new drug is better than the standard?
questions.rationale: Phase I safety and dosage; II effectiveness; III comparison with standard drug; IV post-marketing.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Clinical Trials (PDF p. 106)
questions.quote: PHASE III Establish if new drug is more effective than the standard drug.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A nurse is asked to give a medicine another nurse prepared. What should she do?
questions.rationale: Do not administer any medication you did not prepare.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Nursing Responsibilities (PDF p. 106)
questions.quote: Do not administer any medication that you did not prepare.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which drug group is OTOTOXIC?
questions.rationale: Ototoxic drugs include aminoglycosides, aspirin, chloroquine, and loop diuretics.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Drug Toxicities (PDF p. 106)
questions.quote: Ototoxic drugs Aminoglycosides

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which drug causes a disulfiram-like reaction with alcohol?
questions.rationale: Metronidazole, some cephalosporins, and oral hypoglycemics cause disulfiram reactions.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Drug Reactions (PDF p. 107)
questions.quote: Disulfiram reaction Metronidazole

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Beta-2 receptors are found mainly in the:
questions.rationale: Beta-1 receptors are in the heart; beta-2 in the bronchi, vascular and uterine smooth muscle.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Adrenergic Receptors (PDF p. 107)
questions.quote: Bronchi, smooth muscles in the blood vessels, uterine muscles

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which effect is caused by SYMPATHETIC stimulation?
questions.rationale: Sympathetic effects: mydriasis, bronchodilation, increased HR, decreased peristalsis, bladder relaxation.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, ANS Responses (PDF p. 107)
questions.quote: Bronchioles Bronchodilate Bronchoconstrict

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which drug is used first in anaphylaxis?
questions.rationale: Epinephrine treats anaphylaxis, bronchospasm, and cardiac arrest.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Adrenergic Drugs (PDF p. 108)
questions.quote: Treats Allergic reaction, anaphylaxis, bronchospasm & cardiac arrest

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Combining albuterol with which drug class risks hypertensive crisis?
questions.rationale: Albuterol with MAOIs can cause hypertensive crisis.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Adrenergic Drugs (PDF p. 108)
questions.quote: Should not be given with MAOI (can cause hypertensive crisis)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which antidote is used for norepinephrine or dopamine extravasation/overdose?
questions.rationale: Phentolamine is the antidote for norepinephrine and dopamine overdose or extravasation.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Adrenergic Drugs (PDF p. 108)
questions.quote: Phentolamine mesylate = antidote for NE and dopamine overdose

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Non-selective beta blockers like propranolol are used cautiously in which client?
questions.rationale: Non-selective beta blockers can cause bronchospasm; caution in COPD, asthma, and diabetes.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Beta Blockers (PDF p. 108)
questions.quote: Bronchial Asthma

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which is a CARDIOSELECTIVE (beta-1) blocker?
questions.rationale: Selective beta-1 blockers include metoprolol, atenolol, acebutolol, betaxolol, and esmolol.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Beta Blockers (PDF p. 109)
questions.quote: Metoprolol

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Bethanechol is given to treat:
questions.rationale: Bethanechol, a direct cholinergic agonist, treats urinary retention and abdominal distention.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Cholinergic Agonists (PDF p. 109)
questions.quote: Used to treat urinary retention and abdominal distention

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What is the antidote for cholinergic overdose?
questions.rationale: Atropine counters cholinergic overdose (salivation, sweating, cramps). Pralidoxime reverses irreversible cholinesterase inhibitors.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Cholinergic Agonists (PDF p. 109)
questions.quote: ATROPINE SULFATE = antidote for cholinergic overdose

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Pralidoxime is the antidote for poisoning with which agents?
questions.rationale: Pralidoxime reverses irreversible acetylcholinesterase inhibitors such as organophosphate pesticides.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Cholinergic Agonists (PDF p. 109)
questions.quote: PRALIDOXIME = antidote for irreversible acetylcholinesterase-inhibiting drugs

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which is a sign of cholinergic excess (SLUDGE)?
questions.rationale: SLUDGE: salivation, lacrimation, urinary incontinence, diarrhea, GI cramps, emesis.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Cholinergic Effects (PDF p. 109)
questions.quote: D - iarrhea

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which teaching is specific to phenytoin?
options: Good oral hygiene and dental visits
questions.rationale: Phenytoin causes gingival hyperplasia, so oral hygiene and dental visits are stressed; it is not mixed with other IV fluids.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Anticonvulsants (PDF p. 110)
questions.quote: Phenytoin: good oral hygiene, frequent dental visits

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Why is carbidopa combined with levodopa?
questions.rationale: Carbidopa inhibits peripheral dopa decarboxylase so more levodopa reaches the brain.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Anti-Parkinson Agents (PDF p. 110)
questions.quote: Inhibits the enzyme dopa decarboxylase
